claude_take: Today's throughline is control: Skydance tightening its grip on Warner Bros.' creative leadership, Frasers Group inching toward becoming Burberry's biggest shareholder, and Disney picking through Character.AI's bankrupt estate for the IP it spent years fighting in court. Reese Witherspoon's buyback of Hello Sunshine reads like the rare exception - a founder clawing ownership back rather than ceding it. And it's hard to ignore the gap between Google rushing Gemini 4 Argon out to millions of subscribers and Pew's finding that nearly half of Americans can't cover a basic expense without strain: the technology keeps scaling up just as the margin for everyone else keeps shrinking.
claude_take_title: A Founder Claws Back What Finance Took

items.headline: Google Opens Gemini 4 Argon to the Public via the Gemini App
items.summary: Google has rolled out its flagship Gemini 4 Argon model to Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in Search, after weeks of limiting access to vetted cybersecurity defenders. Developers can also reach it through a paid Gemini API tier, while Google AI Studio and the Antigravity coding tools remain Ultra-only for now. The expansion marks Google's most direct push yet to put its top model in front of mainstream users rather than specialists.

items.headline: Character.AI Files for Bankruptcy, With Disney as the Lead $20 Million Bidder
items.summary: Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware and named a Disney affiliate's stalking-horse bid of $20 million for a non-exclusive IP license as the opening offer in a court-supervised asset sale. The filing caps years of legal pressure from Disney over user-made chatbots impersonating its copyrighted characters, and Disney has already hired the startup's former CEO as its first chief technology officer. If no better offer emerges by late November, the platform could be wound down entirely.

items.headline: Reese Witherspoon Buys Back Hello Sunshine From Candle Media
items.summary: Witherspoon is teaming with the Paris-based Mediawan to reacquire Hello Sunshine, the production company she sold to Candle Media for roughly $900 million in 2021. The move returns the company, known for adaptations like 'Gone Girl' and 'Little Fires Everywhere,' to creator-led ownership and comes as Candle Media continues stepping back from its original plan to build and eventually sell an integrated media company.

items.headline: Skydance Ousts Warner Bros. Film Chiefs Pamela Abdy and Michael De Luca
items.summary: Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has removed Warner Bros.' film division leaders Pamela Abdy and Michael De Luca, handing control of both studios' film labels to Skydance executives Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein. The exits follow Ellison's memo warning staff of 'difficult decisions' as the merged company chases more than $6 billion in savings, and cap a four-year run at Warner Bros. that included Oscar winners 'Sinners' and 'One Battle After Another' alongside costly flops like 'Joker: Folie a Deux.'

items.headline: Pope Leo XIV Diagnosed With Lung Cancer After Surgery
items.summary: The Vatican said tests confirmed lung adenocarcinoma after surgeons removed the lower lobe of Pope Leo XIV's right lung in a 90-minute operation at Rome's Gemelli Hospital. Doctors called the surgery successful with no complications, though staging and whether further treatment is needed remain unclear. The Vatican has canceled the pope's audiences through October 20 and has not said whether a planned trip to South America will go ahead.

items.headline: Pew: Nearly Half of Americans Struggled to Afford a Basic Necessity This Year
items.summary: A new Pew Research Center survey finds 44% of U.S. adults had trouble paying for at least one basic necessity, such as food, housing or healthcare, in the past year, with lower-income adults hit hardest. The survey also found 53% of Americans lack enough savings to cover three months of expenses in an emergency, underscoring a broad sense of financial precarity heading into the midterms.

items.headline: Frasers Group Raises Its Burberry Stake to 7.42%
items.summary: Mike Ashley's Frasers Group has increased its voting-rights interest in Burberry to 7.42%, up from 6.32% a month earlier, built entirely through derivative instruments rather than direct share purchases. If the underlying put options were exercised, Frasers would become Burberry's largest investor, extending a luxury push that already includes a roughly 48% stake in Hugo Boss. Burberry has not commented, and Frasers has not announced any takeover intention.

items.headline: Wittgenstein's Language Games
items.headline_fr: Les jeux de langage de Wittgenstein
items.summary: Ludwig Wittgenstein argued in his later work that the meaning of words comes not from some fixed link between word and object, but from how words are actually used within a shared social practice, or 'language game,' with its own rules - much like the meaning of a chess piece lies in how it moves, not in its shape. This broke from his own earlier picture-theory of language and from much of Western philosophy's search for fixed essences. The idea still matters because it explains why words shift meaning across contexts (a 'cloud' means something different to a meteorologist and a software engineer), and why trying to pin down a single, context-free definition for contested terms often misses the point entirely.
items.summary_fr: Dans ses derniers travaux, Wittgenstein soutient que le sens des mots ne vient pas d'un lien fixe entre le mot et la chose, mais de la façon dont ils sont effectivement utilisés au sein d'une pratique sociale partagée, un « jeu de langage » doté de ses propres règles, tout comme la valeur d'une pièce d'échecs tient à son usage et non à sa forme. Cette idée rompt avec sa propre théorie du langage de jeunesse et avec une grande partie de la philosophie occidentale en quête d'essences fixes. Elle reste précieuse aujourd'hui car elle explique pourquoi un même mot change de sens selon le contexte, et pourquoi vouloir figer une définition unique de notions contestées passe souvent à côté de l'essentiel.
